name: High-Bay Lighting Waste
applicable_contexts: long runtime or intermittent occupancy plausible
trigger_conditions: high-bay lighting inventory or large open floor area plausible
anti_triggers: continuous lighting is operationally required and evidenced
advanced lighting controls confirmed and functioning
physical_basis: Large high-bay spaces can accumulate avoidable lighting runtime when schedule, zoning and occupancy are not aligned.
operational_basis: Crude schedules, overrides or weak zoning can keep large lighting loads active outside productive or service-relevant windows.
financial_mechanism: Lighting runtime can add avoidable kWh and sometimes peak contribution, creating a misleading whole-building efficiency story.
typical_false_assumption: If lighting is visible, the right answer is immediate fixture CAPEX.
hypothesis: High-bay lighting runtime or controls drift may create avoidable load before equipment-replacement logic is justified.
rival_hypotheses: runtime is already aligned to occupancy and service windows
lighting is non-material relative to charging, HVAC or process duty
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: runtime materially exceeds occupied or service-relevant hours
controls absence, bypass or drift evidenced
falsification_conditions: lighting already zoned and controlled to actual use
allowed_claim_language: High-bay lighting waste is a plausible hypothesis requiring schedule and controls validation.
prohibited_claim_language: This asset is wasting energy through high-bay lighting.
financial_exposure_if_true: lighting CAPEX sequencing may be misread
controls-first action may outperform equipment-first action
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to rival drivers
stop_conditions: lighting runtime and controls maturity are bounded enough to rank the hypothesis
escalation_conditions: operator schedule confirmation required if public evidence remains thin
claim_permissions_impact: block fixture-replacement recommendation without runtime evidence
example_outputs: Before replacing fixtures, determine whether lighting runtime is actually following occupancy and service windows.
tests: warehouse and logistics cases with large high-bay area should admit this as a bounded loss hypothesis
no direct local-loss statement allowed without case evidence
